title: Lansdown Hill, Beckford's Tower and Bath Racecourse Walk Route

images.title: Daderot, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Beckford's Tower. The tower was built for William Thomas Beckford, a wealthy novelist, art collector and critic, to designs by Henry Goodridge, and was completed in 1827. Beckford used it as a library and a retreat, with the cupola at the top acting as a belvedere providing views over the surrounding countryside. The Italianate building at the base of the tower housed drawing rooms and a library. Extensive grounds between Beckford's house in Lansdown Crescent and the tower were landscaped and planted to create Beckford's Ride. It is now home to a museum displaying furniture originally made for the tower and paintings, prints and objects illustrating Beckford's life as a writer, collector and patron of the arts.

description: This circular walk explores a lovely area to the north of the city of Bath. On the route you will climb to a fine viewpoint, visit a Grade I listed tower and explore the public footpaths that cross Bath Racecourse. The route leads through lush hillside pastures, passing Beckford's Tower, a former novelist's retreat, before crossing playing fields to reach Bath Racecourse. A loop around the racecourse includes a stop at the toposcope viewpoint at Prospect Stile, which provides far-reaching vistas over Bath, Bristol, and the surrounding area. Please note the racecourse paths are not open to the public on race days. The Cotswold Way National Trail passes over Prospect Stile. You could pick up the waymarked trail to extend your walk. Just to the west there's another fine local climb to Kelston Roundhill .
